stem: Far-end plants dry faster than near-end plants on the same schedule. Which check best tests a delivery hypothesis?
choices: Raise nutrient concentration slightly for the far-end plants because faster dryback indicates higher plant demand.
Increase event duration room-wide and use substrate response to determine whether the distribution problem improves.
Compare cultivar/root-zone demand first because the same irrigation schedule can produce different dryback even with equal delivery.
Measure representative emitter output and relevant pressure/filtration conditions across near, far, and affected positions in the zone.
rationale: A near-versus-far dryback pattern creates a plausible hydraulic-distribution hypothesis. Directly measuring emitter output, pressure, and filtration condition across the zone tests whether the irrigation system is actually delivering less water where the plants dry faster. Changing recipe or duration before measuring distribution adds another variable, while cultivar demand may contribute but does not explain a measured delivery difference if one exists.
